bull.b: Braze is still scaling at a strong rate, with management guiding to approximately 23% full-year growth and reporting 26% second-quarter growth. Continued expansion provides a durable base for operating leverage, broader customer adoption, and increasing relevance in enterprise marketing software.

Positive and growing free cash flow strengthens Braze’s ability to fund product development, sales capacity, and AI innovation without relying as heavily on external capital. The improvement from previously negative free cash flow also indicates better operating discipline and cash conversion.

Net retention above 100% shows that existing customers are expanding their spending, supporting recurring revenue durability beyond new-logo growth. Strong large-account retention and deeper platform adoption can increase switching costs and create further opportunities to sell additional channels and AI products.

bear.b: Braze has not yet converted its strong revenue growth and healthy gross margin into sustained GAAP profitability. Continued net and operating losses reduce the resilience of earnings, constrain internally funded investment, and leave execution dependent on further efficiency gains and scale.

Gross-margin pressure from premium messaging and added Decisioning Studio costs could limit the operating leverage expected from software scale. If these costs persist as usage and AI adoption grow, Braze may need stronger pricing, mix improvement, or productivity gains to protect profitability.

The ongoing pricing and packaging migration creates execution risk across customer contracts, revenue classification, and year-over-year comparisons. Reclassifying some subscription revenue as professional services may obscure underlying trends and require careful management to preserve customer retention and expansion.
